title: Harnessing Generative AI (GenAI) for Automated Feedback in Higher Education: A Systematic Review
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the emerging use of generative AI for automated feedback in higher education. The authors note that higher education instructors face growing pressure to provide timely, personalized, and scalable feedback, especially in online and large-enrollment courses. Prior reviews had examined automated feedback or generative AI separately, but had not focused specifically on GenAI-based feedback in higher education or on how these systems are implemented in authentic instructional settings. The review therefore asks three questions: what contexts GenAI feedback systems are used in, what their main characteristics are, and what possibilities they create for higher education.

The authors conducted a systematic review following PRISMA-style procedures and Arksey and O'Malley's framework. They searched peer-reviewed English-language journal articles published from 2019 to 2023 in Academic Search Premier and Education Source, screened 1,976 non-duplicate records, and ultimately included 10 empirical studies from Q1 or Q2 journals. The reviewed studies examined GenAI-based feedback tools such as ChatGPT, chatbots, digital tutors, and specialized writing/assessment systems. These tools were used for automated feedback in contexts including language learning, academic writing, creative thinking, and STEM courses. Across the reviewed studies, GenAI systems served purposes such as personalized learning, collaborative problem-solving, self-regulated learning, and motivation/engagement.

The population and context are higher education settings, including undergraduate and some graduate-level contexts, with both students and educators implicated in implementation. The review synthesizes studies conducted in varied instructional environments, with frequent relevance to online learning and large-scale courses. It also emphasizes instructor roles in implementation, including guiding students' use of GenAI, providing higher-level or final feedback, engineering prompts, and facilitating deeper learning beyond what automated systems can provide.

The main conclusions are that GenAI automated feedback systems show strong promise for improving educational efficiency and support in higher education. The reviewed evidence suggests these systems can reduce instructor workload, provide timely and personalized feedback, improve communication, support cognitive and emotional needs, and expand access to feedback in lower-pressure environments. At the same time, the review highlights unresolved issues such as ethical concerns, accuracy, overreliance, and the need to better define instructors' roles in AI-supported feedback ecosystems. The authors conclude that GenAI should be integrated in ways that augment rather than replace human instruction, and they call for more research as the field develops.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI automated feedback systems in higher education, including chatbots, LLM-based writing assessment tools, and course-integrated feedback agents used across multiple studies.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper systematically reviews 10 empirical higher-education studies (2019-2023) on GenAI for automated feedback, synthesizing how such systems were used for writing, language learning, creative thinking, and STEM feedback/support.

findings.finding_summary: Across the 10 reviewed studies, the authors conclude that GenAI automated feedback systems improved educational outcomes in varied higher-education contexts, especially via personalized learning, collaborative problem-solving, self-regulated learning, and motivation/engagement. No pooled effect size, confidence interval, or aggregate sample size was reported.
findings.measure: Educational outcomes across reviewed studies, including learning outcomes, writing/argumentation performance, self-regulated learning, motivation, and engagement

findings.finding_summary: The review finds that GenAI systems can reduce instructor workload by automating routine grading and feedback tasks, especially in language learning and writing contexts. This allows instructors to focus on more complex teaching responsibilities, though no pooled quantitative workload estimate was reported.
findings.measure: Instructor workload reduction / automation of grading and feedback tasks

findings.finding_summary: The authors synthesize evidence that GenAI feedback systems can provide cognitive and emotional support by creating comfortable, low-pressure, supportive learning environments that encourage help-seeking and engagement. These benefits were described qualitatively across included studies without pooled effect sizes or aggregate sample sizes.
findings.measure: Emotional support, stress reduction, comfort seeking help, engagement with feedback

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that GenAI feedback systems enhance communication and accessibility within courses by enabling real-time, on-demand support among students, instructors, and teaching assistants. Findings were synthesized narratively across studies and no pooled institutional effect metrics were reported.
findings.measure: Communication, accessibility, and support processes in higher-education learning environments

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review of 10 empirical peer-reviewed studies in Q1/Q2 journals, which is stronger than a single primary study. However, it is not a quantitative meta-analysis and reports narrative synthesis without pooled effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports broadly positive impacts on student outcomes, support, and instructor efficiency, but effect sizes and aggregate sample sizes are not reported. Impact is therefore promising but unclear in magnitude.
